doc: Cross-reference blocks and prose notes held once, referenced by key from data/media/<id>.json. Join components[].xref_id on 'xrefs'; join components[].xref_note_id and components[].mapping_note_id on 'notes'. An absent xref_id means the component has no cross-references, not that they live elsewhere. tools/refs.py:resolve_component() performs the join and reconstructs the flat record exactly.
xref_semantics: A cross-reference block describes the BiGG id that was CHOSEN for the component. Whether it was also the evidence for that choice is stated per component by match_field / match_key / source_xref, and by the note referenced from xref_note_id, not by this table.

notes.n0b5208: [MIX-SOLN-01] A named multi-compound stock solution is not one metabolite. Wolfe's mineral solution (14 salts) had been collapsed onto molybdate alone; a Wolin/DSM-141 vitamin solution (10 vitamins) onto folate alone; a nine-vitamin string onto pyridoxine alone. The generating code (tools/enrich_coverage.py recover(), which returns on the FIRST token that maps and discards the rest) silently deleted every remaining constituent. A stock solution must be expanded into its constituents as a declared approximation, or left unmapped -- never reduced to whichever member matched first. The pattern is ANCHORED at the start of the name: a component named for ONE ion that merely annotates which stock it came from ("Copper (trace element solution)", "Biotin (Wolfe's vitamins)") is a correctly decomposed constituent and must be left alone -- an unanchored pattern deleted ~50 such rows in testing.

The alias entries that produced it have been removed from tools/map_metabolite.py.

"PUFA 18:3 n-3 c,c,c (ALA)" is excluded and keeps its name tier.; [CHEM-GLA-01] C18:3 n-6 is GAMMA-linolenic acid (lnlncg, C18H29O2, InChIKey VZCCETWTMQHEPK-QNEBEIHSSA-M, in BiGGr). It had been mapped to lnlnca, ALPHA-linolenic acid, which is C18:3 n-3 -- the same chain length and degree of unsaturation but different double-bond positions, so a different compound with a different InChIKey (DTOSIQBPPRVQHS-PDBXOOCHSA-M). The n-3/n-6 distinction is the whole point of reporting these separately. Also corrected in the mapper alias table.

Cyanocobalamin (C63H88CoN14O14P) has no in_biggr BiGG id (b12 carries no formula and no InChIKey and is absent from BiGGr). adocbl (Adenosylcobalamin, C72H100CoN18O17P, ZIHHMGTYZOSFRC-QRVZQHAISA-N) is a real dietary/coenzyme B12 form present in BiGGr and is recorded as a declared proxy for the vitamer group, not as an exact identity.
